edgekws-2-0-low-latency-voice-activator-.problem: Develop an on-device keyword spotting system for the wake word 'Dear Folk' using ESP32-S3 and INMP441 microphone to enable low-latency voice activation without continuous audio transmission to remote servers, reducing bandwidth and latency while operating under tight hardware and budget constraints.

functional_requirements.title: Wake Word Detection
functional_requirements.description: The system must detect the wake word 'Dear Folk' from 16 kHz I2S audio input using an INT8 TensorFlow Lite Micro model with inference latency under 200 ms.

functional_requirements.title: Audio Capture and Preprocessing
functional_requirements.description: The system must capture mono audio via I2S from INMP441 microphone at 16 kHz, apply necessary preprocessing (e.g., framing, normalization) compatible with the TFLite model input format.

functional_requirements.title: Post-Detection Activation
functional_requirements.description: Upon wake word detection, the system must trigger a signal to enable audio streaming to a remote ASR service (e.g., via Firebase or HTTP) within 50 ms of detection.

functional_requirements.title: Model Inference on ESP32-S3
functional_requirements.description: The INT8 TFLite model must run entirely on the ESP32-S3 using TensorFlow Lite Micro, with peak RAM usage under 256 KB and CPU utilization allowing real-time processing.

functional_requirements.title: Low-Power Operation
functional_requirements.description: The system must minimize power consumption during idle listening, aiming for average current draw under 15 mA to support battery-operated edge deployment.

non_functional_requirements.title: Latency Requirement
non_functional_requirements.description: End-to-end latency from wake word utterance to detection signal must not exceed 300 ms to ensure responsive user interaction.

non_functional_requirements.title: Model Size Constraint
non_functional_requirements.description: The quantized INT8 TensorFlow Lite model must fit within the ESP32-S3's available RAM (≤ 512 KB) and flash (≤ 4 MB) to allow room for OS and audio buffers.

non_functional_requirements.title: Robustness to Noise
non_functional_requirements.description: The system must maintain ≥ 80% true positive rate and ≤ 10% false accept rate in mild background noise (e.g., 60 dB ambient) to ensure usability in real environments.

non_functional_requirements.title: Development and Deployment Simplicity
non_functional_requirements.description: The system must be programmable using Arduino IDE or PlatformIO with minimal external dependencies to support student developers and rapid iteration.

constraints: ESP32-S3 limited RAM (~512 KB) and processing power for real-time audio inference
Student budget restricts access to premium hardware or cloud training resources
Limited training data for the wake word 'Dear Folk' may affect model accuracy
Real-time audio processing requires deterministic timing and I2S DMA reliability
INT8 quantization must preserve model accuracy while enabling deployment on microcontroller
assumptions: The INMP441 microphone provides stable 16-bit I2S audio at 16 kHz without significant hardware noise or dropout
An INT8 TFLite model for 'Dear Folk' can be trained or converted to achieve acceptable accuracy (>80% TP, <10% FA) with limited data
Firebase or similar service can be used for lightweight signaling or audio upload post-detection without complex authentication overhead
open_questions: What is the minimum acceptable model size and architecture (e.g., depthwise separable CNN) that achieves target accuracy on 'Dear Folk' with INT8 quantization?
How will false activations be mitigated in noisy environments without significantly increasing latency or power consumption?
What is the optimal audio buffering strategy (frame size, hop length) to balance latency, memory use, and feature extraction quality for keyword spotting on ESP32-S3?

smart-campus-parking-system-178983972637.summary: Architecture is coherent and budget-aware, but three open questions create material execution risk. Sensor selection, deployment environment, and dashboard responsiveness must be resolved in Week 1 to avoid schedule overrun or cost breach.

risks.title: Undecided deployment environment (indoor vs outdoor)
risks.detail: Affects enclosure IP rating, power source (solar vs mains), sensor mounting, and BOM cost. Wrong assumption could blow ₹4k budget or require rework.
risks.recommendation: Confirm demo location with stakeholder in Week 1; procure IP65 boxes + solar only if outdoor.

risks.title: Sensor type not finalized
risks.detail: Ultrasonic vs IR vs magnetic impacts cost, accuracy, false-positive rate, and mounting. HC-SR04 assumed in BOM but not validated for chosen environment.
risks.recommendation: Bench-test HC-SR04 and IR module in Week 1; select based on false-positive rate and cost fit.

risks.title: Firebase Spark plan quota exhaustion
risks.detail: Free tier limits (100 simultaneous connections, 1 GB stored, 10 GB/month egress) may be exceeded by 4 nodes + dashboard + 90-day history, causing data loss or latency spikes.
risks.recommendation: Estimate daily writes/reads; implement client-side throttling and Firestore TTL cleanup; monitor usage dashboard weekly.

risks.title: Offline buffering implementation gap
risks.detail: Architecture states ESP32 buffers 50 events locally, but no detail on storage (NVS vs SPIFFS), persistence across power loss, or sync conflict resolution on reconnect.
risks.recommendation: Define local storage mechanism and replay logic in Week 1; add integration test for Wi-Fi outage/recovery scenario.

risks.title: Mobile-responsive dashboard scope creep
risks.detail: Responsive CSS adds ~1 week effort; 6-week schedule leaves minimal buffer. Desktop-only MVP keeps schedule intact.
risks.recommendation: Agree on desktop-only MVP with stakeholder; treat responsive as stretch goal after core features pass acceptance.

ai-based-smart-water-tank-monitoring-sys.summary: Architecture is coherent for a low-cost prototype but has critical gaps in sensor selection for accuracy, power budget validation, Firebase cost/limits on Spark plan, OTA security, and missing calibration strategy.

risks.title: Ultrasonic sensor accuracy vs ±2% requirement
risks.detail: HC-SR04/JSN-SR04T typical error is ±3 mm plus temperature drift; on a 3 m tank this exceeds ±2% (60 mm). No temperature compensation or calibration procedure defined.
risks.recommendation: Add DS18B20 for temperature compensation, implement two-point calibration in firmware, and validate error budget before finalizing sensor choice.

risks.title: Power budget unvalidated for <100 mA average
risks.detail: Architecture assumes deep sleep meets target but omits Wi-Fi reconnection energy, sensor current, LDO quiescent loss, and battery self-discharge. No energy model or measurement plan exists.
risks.recommendation: Build an energy spreadsheet (active ms, sleep µA, Wi-Fi reconnect J), measure on bench with a current profiler, and size battery/solar for worst-case winter.

risks.title: Firebase Spark plan limits may break persistence & OTA
risks.detail: Spark plan caps: 1 GB Realtime DB, 50k Firestore reads/day, 10 GB Hosting bandwidth. 30-day history at 1-min intervals = 43k writes + dashboard reads; OTA binaries consume Hosting bandwidth. Risk of quota exhaustion.
risks.recommendation: Calculate daily ops: readings, dashboard polls, OTA pulls. Add data retention policy (e.g., 7-day high-res, 30-day downsampled). Plan fallback to paid tier or local SD card logging.

risks.title: OTA update mechanism lacks integrity & rollback
risks.detail: Architecture uses plain HTTP GET from Firebase Hosting for firmware binary. No signature verification, version check, or rollback on failed boot. A corrupted or malicious binary bricks the device.
risks.recommendation: Implement signed firmware (RSA/ECDSA), secure boot, version manifest with min-version enforcement, and dual-bank OTA with automatic rollback on boot failure.

risks.title: No calibration/installation procedure for tank geometry
risks.detail: Water level % depends on exact sensor mounting height, tank shape, and dead zones. Requirements assume configurable tank height but no calibration workflow, leading to systematic offset errors.
risks.recommendation: Add a one-time calibration mode: measure empty/full distances, store in NVS, expose via dashboard. Document sensor mounting constraints (beam angle, obstructions).

ai-based-smart-water-tank-monitoring-sys.summary: Verification strategy covers sensor accuracy, threshold alerts, real-time dashboard latency, data persistence, offline queuing, power efficiency, OTA updates, and cost validation. Tests are designed for a single-tank prototype using ESP32, ultrasonic sensor, Firebase, and React dashboard.

test_cases.scenario: Water level measurement accuracy across full tank range
test_cases.precondition: Tank empty, sensor mounted at top, ESP32 powered and calibrated with known tank height
test_cases.expected_result: Reported level percentage matches physical water level within ±2% of tank height at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% fill levels

test_cases.scenario: Low-water and overflow threshold alerts trigger correctly
test_cases.precondition: Thresholds configured (e.g., low=20%, high=95%), tank at 50% level, system running
test_cases.expected_result: Low alert activates when level drops below 20%, overflow alert activates when level exceeds 95%, both clear when level returns to normal range

test_cases.scenario: Real-time dashboard updates within 5 seconds of sensor reading
test_cases.precondition: Dashboard open in browser, ESP32 online and taking readings at configured interval
test_cases.expected_result: Dashboard displays new level percentage and alert status within 5 seconds of ESP32 pushing to Firebase Realtime Database

test_cases.scenario: Historical data persistence and 30-day trend display
test_cases.precondition: System running for >24 hours with multiple readings stored in Firestore
test_cases.expected_result: Dashboard trend chart shows timestamped readings for past 30 days; data query returns correct values matching ESP32 logs

test_cases.scenario: Offline queuing and sync after Wi-Fi outage
test_cases.precondition: ESP32 running, Wi-Fi disconnected for 10 minutes, then restored
test_cases.expected_result: Readings taken during outage are queued locally; after reconnect, all queued readings appear in Firestore with correct timestamps, no data loss

test_cases.scenario: Power efficiency meets <100 mA average current draw
test_cases.precondition: ESP32 in deep sleep between readings (e.g., 5 min interval), powered by battery, multimeter in series
test_cases.expected_result: Average current over 1 hour ≤ 100 mA, confirming battery/solar viability

test_cases.scenario: OTA firmware update via Firebase Hosting
test_cases.precondition: New firmware binary uploaded to Firebase Hosting, ESP32 running older version, OTA trigger enabled
test_cases.expected_result: ESP32 downloads and flashes new firmware successfully, reboots, and resumes normal operation with new version

test_cases.scenario: Total bill of materials cost validation
test_cases.precondition: All components procured for single prototype (ESP32, sensor, power, enclosure, misc)
test_cases.expected_result: Total cost ≤ ₹4,000 as per budget constraint

waste2shield-1789843978721.summary: Execution plan for Waste2Shield IoT prototype: resolve critical Wi-Fi connectivity and data gaps first, then build sensor node firmware, Firebase backend, React dashboard, and OTA pipeline in dependency order within 8-week student timeline.

milestones.title: Feasibility & Data Foundation
milestones.description: Validate campus Wi-Fi connectivity for ESP32 and collect labeled sensor dataset for target waste streams.

milestones.title: Core System Implementation
milestones.description: Develop ESP32 firmware with sensor acquisition, TFLite inference, and Firebase sync; deploy Firebase backend with alerting; build React dashboard with live charts and overrides.

milestones.title: Integration, OTA & Field Test
milestones.description: Implement OTA pipeline, integrate all components, run end-to-end field test with 2-3 nodes, and document results.

tasks.title: Test ESP32 Wi-Fi on campus APs & design fallback
tasks.description: Connect ESP32 to target campus Wi-Fi SSIDs; verify captive portal behavior. If blocked, prototype ESP-NOW gateway bridge to Ethernet.
success_criteria: ESP32 obtains IP and reaches Firebase HTTPS endpoint
Fallback gateway design documented if needed

tasks.title: Collect labeled sensor dataset & finalize waste classes
tasks.description: Gather 200+ samples per class (food, PET, hazardous) using sensor node breadboard; label with ground truth; agree final class list with stakeholder.
success_criteria: CSV dataset with ≥200 rows per class
Stakeholder sign-off on class labels

tasks.title: Develop ESP32 firmware: sensor drivers, deep-sleep, TFLite inference
tasks.description: Write FreeRTOS tasks for BME680, VL53L0X, HX711 at 1 Hz; implement 55 s/5 s deep-sleep cycle; integrate quantized TFLite model; log to serial for debug.
success_criteria: All sensors read successfully at 1 Hz
Inference latency < 200 ms
Average current ≤ 80 mA measured

tasks.title: Implement Firebase backend: Realtime DB, Firestore, Auth, Cloud Functions
tasks.description: Provision Firebase project; create telemetry/alerts/commands data structure; write Cloud Function for threshold alerting (push/email); configure Spark plan quotas.
success_criteria: Telemetry writes visible in console < 2 s
Alert function triggers on test threshold breach
Auth rules restrict write to node UIDs

tasks.title: Integrate ESP32 Wi-Fi + Firebase HTTPS/WS sync
tasks.description: Add Wi-Fi manager, TLS certs, HTTPS POST to Firestore and WebSocket listener for Realtime DB; implement command polling on wake; handle reconnection/backoff.
success_criteria: End-to-end sensor-to-dashboard latency ≤ 3 s
Node recovers from Wi-Fi drop automatically
Battery life target met with network duty cycle

tasks.title: Build React dashboard: live charts, classification view, override controls
tasks.description: Scaffold Vite+React+Firebase SDK; create Chart.js components for temp/gas/level; show classification confidence & fill forecast; add Firestore command writer for reboot/sleep/calibrate.
success_criteria: Dashboard updates < 1 s after node push
Override command appears in Firestore within 500 ms
PWA installs on mobile

tasks.title: Implement OTA pipeline: GitHub Actions → Firebase Storage → ESP32 HTTPS OTA
tasks.description: Add RSA-2048 signing to firmware build; GitHub Action uploads signed .bin + version.json to Firebase Storage; ESP32 verifies signature on boot and flashes.
success_criteria: CI produces signed binary on tag push
Node downloads & verifies signature
Successful flash without brick on test update

tasks.title: End-to-end field test with 2-3 nodes & documentation
tasks.description: Deploy 2-3 assembled nodes at waste sites; run 48 h continuous; capture latency, battery, accuracy, alert reliability; write final report & repo README.
success_criteria: All nodes online > 95 % of test period
Classification accuracy ≥ 85 % on field data
Dashboard shows live data & alerts correctly
Total BOM ≤ $35/node documented

planning_notes: Task-1 (Wi-Fi) and Task-2 (dataset) can run in parallel week 1-2.
If campus Wi-Fi blocks ESP32, Task-1 fallback adds ~1 week; compress Task-3/5 by using ESP-NOW gateway.
Firebase Spark quota: batch telemetry every 10 s in Task-5 to stay within free tier.
OTA (Task-7) depends on firmware stability from Task-3; schedule after first working node.

edgekws-2-0-low-latency-voice-activator-.name: EdgeKWS 2.0 – Low-Latency Voice Activator for Edge Devices
edgekws-2-0-low-latency-voice-activator-.idea: Develop an on-device keyword spotting system that detects the wake word “Dear Folk” directly from microphone audio without continuously sending audio to a remote server. The system uses an ESP32-S3 with an INMP441 I2S microphone and an INT8 TensorFlow Lite model to perform low-latency voice activation. After detecting the wake word, the system can activate subsequent audio streaming to a remote speech-recognition service, reducing unnecessary transmission, latency, and bandwidth usage
edgekws-2-0-low-latency-voice-activator-.objective: To build and validate a lightweight, low-latency keyword-spotting system capable of reliably detecting the wake word “Dear Folk” on an edge device, with low memory and computational requirements, before activating further voice processing or remote ASR.
edgekws-2-0-low-latency-voice-activator-.constraints: Limited hardware access, student budget, ESP32-S3 memory and processing constraints, real-time audio processing requirements, 16 kHz audio sampling, limited training data, and the need for low-latency inference with a lightweight INT8 model
